about: Rice Law is a personal injury firm with offices in Timonium, Baltimore and Wheaton.

The firm states that it works on a contingency fee, with nothing to pay unless the case is won; the first consultation is free; its intake line is open around the clock; it will visit clients in hospital or at home.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 2 listings, counts summed and rating weighted by count

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours, photo count and description come from the Places API. The services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way.

ahrefs.source: Ahrefs Site Explorer, batch endpoint, subdomains mode, organic figures for the United States

G1.evidence: Maryland does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.source: Published decisions of the Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland, indexed by CourtListener (Free Law Project)
G2.evidence: No attorney this firm names appears as the respondent in any of the 2614 published discipline decisions of the Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland, 1976 to 2026. 1 of them share a surname with a disciplined attorney and were read against the text of those decisions, which name somebody else. Published decisions record what has been decided, so this covers a disbarment or suspension on the record and not whether a registration is current today.

G3.evidence: 3 physical locations verified on Google Business Profile. Maryland publishes no business register we can query. SDAT's entity search is a form rather than a dataset, its bulk data is sold rather than published, and the state's open data portal carries a count of businesses instead of the register. This is a limit of the published record and not something the firm can change.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 8 named attorneys published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 538 public client reviews across 3 Google listings, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2008-06-28, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP

accountability.evidence: no bar or trial lawyers' association named on the pages we read · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

score.verdict: 3 of 5 eligibility gates passed. 2 could not be answered from the available records (G1, G3) and do not count against the firm. Strongest pillar: B; most headroom in pillar A (0/25).

court_dockets.note: A docket search found 15 case(s) naming this firm alongside sanction or consumer-protection language, none of which is a finding against it: a firm appears in such a docket by arguing about sanctions, or by bringing consumer-protection claims for its clients. Text search over this collection cannot separate an action against a firm from its ordinary practice, so nothing here is settled by it.
